title: Exponential separation in sensing continuous signals via squeezing
authors: Francesco Anna Mele, Nadine Meister, Haimeng Zhao, Senrui Chen, Hsin-Yuan Huang
abstract: Quantum sensing traditionally focuses on using quantum resources such as squeezing and entanglement to improve precision for sensing fixed signals. However, in many applications such as gravitational-wave detection and electromagnetic-field sensing, the signal evolves continuously and varies through time. Additionally, the learner is free to prepare, control, and measure the sensor at arbitrary times, possibly chosen adaptively. In this work, we establish exponential separation in sensing time for continuously evolving signals due to the available squeezing. The signals we study are characterized by a pattern size $T$, and we find that a sensor with squeezing at least $ω(\sqrt{\log T})$ offers a $\mathrm{poly}(T)$ sensing time, whereas those with squeezing at most $o(\sqrt{\log T})$ must use an exponential sensing time in $T$.
summary: This theoretical work quantifies the advantage of quantum squeezing in sensing continuous, time-varying signals. It proves that achieving polynomial sensing time requires the squeezing resource to scale at least as fast as $\omega(\sqrt{\log T})$ relative to the signal pattern size $T$. Below this threshold, the required sensing time explodes exponentially, marking a significant resource-dependent barrier in quantum sensing.
main_problem: The paper establishes a fundamental separation in the required sensing time for continuously evolving quantum signals based on the amount of available quantum squeezing.
main_result: Sufficient squeezing ($z \geq \omega(\sqrt{\log T})$) allows for polynomial sensing time, whereas insufficient squeezing ($z \leq o(\sqrt{\log T})$) forces the sensing time to scale exponentially with the pattern size $T$.
method: The authors analyze the sensing task using Gaussian quantum protocols, comparing the achievable time scaling against theoretical lower bounds derived from information-theoretic arguments.
model_or_system: The system is a single bosonic mode (CV sensor) whose evolution is governed by a time-varying Hamiltonian $\hat{H}(t) = f(t) \hat{p}$, where $f(t)$ represents the unknown, continuously varying signal.

main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the ability to perform adaptive measurements and controls at arbitrary times, which is crucial for establishing the separation boundary.

paper_structure: The paper develops the problem by first setting up the continuous signal model, then establishing the upper bound using Gaussian sensing protocols, and finally deriving the lower bound by showing that any strategy must overcome the exponential barrier unless sufficient squeezing is present.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses the resource scaling in quantum metrology for time-varying signals, providing concrete quantitative thresholds for when simple quantum resources like squeezing provide an exponential advantage over classical or unsqueezed quantum methods.
